concept.name: Lasso regression
concept.definition: Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator: a regularized regression that penalizes the sum of absolute coefficient values, which both shrinks coefficients and sets some exactly to zero, performing continuous variable selection. Introduced by Tibshirani (1996).
concept.intuition: The L1 penalty has corners at zero, so as the penalty tightens the least useful coefficients are pushed exactly to zero and drop out: shrinkage and feature selection in one step.
concept.mechanics: beta_hat minimizes (1/2n) ||y - X beta||^2 + lambda ||beta||_1; there is no closed form, so the path is computed by coordinate descent or LARS with lambda chosen by cross-validation on standardized predictors. The selected model is often refit by OLS (relaxed lasso) to reduce shrinkage bias on the retained coefficients.
concept.formula: beta_hat = argmin_b { (1/2n) sum_i (y_i - x_i' b)^2 + lambda sum_j |b_j| }.
concept.failure_modes: With highly correlated predictors the lasso selects arbitrarily among them, making the selected set unstable across samples, and when p > n it can select at most n variables. Its aggressive selection can drop weak but real predictors.
concept.misconceptions: That lasso selection leaves usual inference intact: p-values computed after data-driven selection are invalid without selective-inference corrections.
concept.example: Screening 200 candidate anomaly signals for return prediction, the lasso path zeroes out all but about 15 signals as lambda decreases, isolating a sparse predictor set.
